intro: Most PM job listings in India ask for 2+ years of experience or an MBA. Straight out of undergrad, the way in is a small set of new-grad programs and a few adjacent roles you can pivot from. Here's the map.

programs.name: Google APM
programs.who: New grads, any degree. Bengaluru cohort.
programs.note: Opens late September, closes late October. ~8,000 applications a year, under 1% taken. Rolling review — apply the day it opens.
programs.mode: Off-campus (open application) — not tied to a specific college list.

programs.name: Microsoft PM (new grad / intern)
programs.note: Campus hiring plus off-campus. Product design and collaboration-heavy interviews.
programs.mode: Both — campus drives at partner colleges, plus an off-campus track.

programs.name: Meta Rotational PM (RPM)
programs.who: New grads. 18 months across three teams.
programs.note: Small cohort, mostly US but takes international grads. Metrics-heavy loop.

programs.name: Flipkart APM
programs.who: Campus hire from select colleges, plus off-campus rounds.
programs.note: Aptitude test, group case, then guesstimate and product rounds. India e-commerce context.
programs.mode: Both — a named campus list, plus an off-campus application form.

programs.name: Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto, Meesho, Razorpay APM
programs.note: A written product teardown or growth problem is usually the main filter. Watch each careers page — cycles are irregular.
programs.mode: Mostly off-campus, posted on each company's own careers page.

programs.name: Atlassian, Uber, Adobe, PhonePe, Groww
programs.who: New-grad APM or PM-I roles, when open.
programs.note: Smaller intakes, often only via campus. Follow them on LinkedIn for the posting.
programs.mode: Mostly campus, at a small set of colleges each cycle.

noProgram.note: If you don't land a program — which is the common case — these roles put you one lateral move from PM.

options.why: Owns the data a PM uses. The most common route into PM in India. Look for it at the same companies.

options.role: Associate PM at an early startup
options.why: Less structured, less competitive, more scope. You'll do real PM work in month one.
Broad exposure to how a company runs. Pivot to PM internally after 12–18 months.

options.role: APM at an agency or services firm
options.why: Lower bar to entry, real client products. Use it to build a portfolio, then move.

misconceptions: Not for an APM program — they hire straight from undergrad. An MBA matters more for switching into PM after a few years in another function.
Helps at Google and for technical products. Plenty of APMs come from other engineering branches, economics, or design.
"I should wait and apply next year with more experience."
The programs are built for people with none. Apply now — you can apply again next cycle if it doesn't work.
